- Rules of the Road","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C - Rules of the Road

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Right-of-way rules set who yields first and the order for entering and crossing intersections, yet nobody ever owns the right of way automatically, so every approach demands a fresh read of the scene [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Yield to the driver who arrived first, to opposing traffic including right-turning vehicles when you turn left, and to the driver on your right when both of you reach a four-way stop at once [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Yield to highway traffic when pulling out of a driveway or private road, to main-road drivers when joining from a minor road, to freeway traffic already rolling when you enter from a ramp, and to any pedestrian, cyclist, or driver still inside the intersection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Control devices span signals, signs, pavement markings, and live direction from officers, highway crews, and school guards, and an officer's orders overrule every sign and signal where two roads meet [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A02
Stacked signals read red over yellow over green from the top, while horizontal city signals read red left, yellow center, and green right, with lone single-color lights posted at some spots [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A02
A green light lets you go straight or turn after yielding to everyone lawfully in the intersection, and a left on green still waits for opposing through traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A02
Yellow warns the signal is turning red, so stop when you safely can; clearing the box on red after a yellow entry is lawful, but entering after red is against the law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
On red, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line until green, then turn right when the way is clear of cars and pedestrians unless a sign bans it [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A02
Left on red is legal only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a full stop and a clear road, and any one-way turn lands in the nearest lane running your direction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow orders slower speed and a sharp watch at crossings, work areas, and service trucks, while a flashing red demands a full stop before moving through clear space [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
Twin flashing reds guard a railroad crossing, so stop until the flashing ends and no train nears, and treat the nearby crossbuck exactly like a yield sign [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
A steady green arrow sends you that way from the proper lane, a flashing yellow arrow urges a careful proceed, an upward green arrow means straight ahead, and a red arrow bans that turn until green, always obeying the head above your lane [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
Warning signs flag possible danger ahead in black on yellow diamonds, urging slower speed and stop readiness, with fluorescent yellow reserved for school zones, school crossings, and pedestrian crossings [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A03
A round yellow board with an X and black railroad letters warns of tracks ahead, so slow down, look, listen, and ready a stop, while the white X that reads Railroad Crossing at the tracks orders a stop behind the line until the way clears [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A03
A posted track count warns that several trains may cross, yet many multi-track crossings carry no such sign and some crossings lack lights entirely, so check every track in both directions yourself [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A03
Cross rails briskly without stopping after looking both ways, wait while a train passes or until gates and lights release you, and when traffic forces a stop, halt at the line ahead of the rails [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A04
Stalled or boxed on the tracks, leave the car at once and run toward the oncoming train and away from the rails to dodge flying debris, then from a safe distance call the 800 number by the crossbuck or call 911, and never restart until a dispatcher says it is safe [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A04
A freight train at 55 miles per hour may need a mile or more to stop, so after one train passes on multi-track rails, wait for a clear view both ways, cross only with room to clear fully, and never stop on the crossing [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A04
Expect a train at every crossing, because rolling past flashing warnings or lowered gates breaks the law and earns a citation [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A04
Orange diamond or rectangular work-zone boards mark construction, maintenance, and emergency work with warnings of crews, slower speeds, detours, slow equipment, and shifting surfaces, so obey flaggers and signs, follow drums, cones, tubes, and temporary signals, and stop at any white line [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A05
Give road workers a brake by slowing down, staying ready for sudden stops, refusing to tailgate, and remembering that work-zone speeding fines double [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A05
Regulatory signs speak the law in white squares, rectangles, or special shapes with black, red, or green markings, covering direction, lanes, turns, speed, and parking, with a red ring and slash banning the pictured act, while black-and-white speed boards cap legal speed for ideal conditions [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A05
An eight-sided red stop sign with white letters orders a stop behind the line or crosswalk plus a yield to crossing traffic and walkers in every direction, and a red-and-white downward triangle yield sign orders slowing until right-of-way traffic passes [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A05
A shared center lane serves left turns from either side only and never through traffic or passing, one-way signs permit travel in the arrow's direction alone, wrong-way signs warn you are headed against traffic at ramps and one-way starts, and do-not-enter signs bar entry at those same spots [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A05
Guide signs in green, brown, or blue squares and rectangles point to crossing roads, towns, sights, hospitals, fuel, food, and lodging [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A06
Route shields use shape and color to name interstate, federal, state, city, county, and local roads, so map your route first and then trail the shields through strange country [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A06
Painted lines, arrows, words, and symbols split lanes, govern passing and lane changes, assign turn lanes, outline walkways, and mark stop points for signs and signals [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A06
Crosswalks frame legal pedestrian crossings, so halt behind the stop line, crosswalk, or sign and yield to anyone entering or inside, stay wary since many crossings lack paint, stop ahead of the intersection when no crossing shows, and honor a stop line before the crosswalk first [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A07
Standard sign colors read red for stop or forbidden, green for permitted movement and guidance, and yellow for general warning [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A08
Standard shapes read horizontal rectangle for guides, lone triangle for yield, vertical rectangle for regulation, diamond for present or possible hazards, pentagon for schools, and round for railroad and advance warning [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0049]
